The pathway indicates that Jerantinine A targets the DNMT3A2/3L complex, which is a component of the DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) enzyme complex. This complex is known to be involved in DNA methylation, a process critical for gene regulation and cellular function. Curguligine B, which is a known inhibitor of the DNMT3A2/3L complex, further supports this interaction, as it is capable of modulating the activity of the DNMT3A2/3L complex. The interaction between Jerantinine A and the DNMT3A2/3L complex, in turn, may lead to a disruption of DNA methylation, potentially affecting the expression of genes regulated by the SLC1B3 transporter. This mechanism implies that Jerantinine A could influence the function of SLC1B3 by altering the activity of the DNMT3A2/3L complex, thereby impacting the transport of organic anions across cellular membranes. The evidence suggests a plausible, mechanistically linked relationship between Jerantinine A and SLC1B3, supported by the known inhibitory effects of Curguligine B on the DNMT3A2/3L complex.
